subject.title: docs: add agent runtime boundary documentation

question: Should the Gateway host teardown and cleanup procedure be a supported public OpenClaw documentation contract, or remain an internal operator runbook with only a short generic public boundary note?
rationale: The issue documents a real maintenance decision, but current source does not establish several host-specific procedures and entrypoint names as OpenClaw product behavior; publishing them makes them user-facing security guidance.

options.title: Narrow public guidance
options.body: Document the generic managed-runtime boundary publicly and keep host-specific wrappers, archive steps, auth-file movement, and cleanup cadence in internal operator docs.

options.title: Adopt full public policy
options.body: Keep the full page after an appropriate Gateway/security owner confirms each normative rule and named runtime as a supported contract.

options.title: Close as internal-only
options.body: Do not add a public page and retain the maintenance record solely in the canonical issue or private operator documentation.

recommendation.title: Narrow public guidance
recommendation.body: Document the generic managed-runtime boundary publicly and keep host-specific wrappers, archive steps, auth-file movement, and cleanup cadence in internal operator docs.

likelyOwner.reason: The available feature-history evidence most directly connects this account to Gateway security and agent-runtime documentation, making it the best routing candidate for the public-policy boundary.
